summary:
Spaceholder is an educational web application designed for long-duration space missions to monitor crew health while addressing NASA’s "Distance from Earth" and "Isolation and Confinement" hazards.

Rather than presenting cold, clinical data dashboards that astronauts often ignore when pushing through fatigue, Spaceholder features a friendly interface driven by an interactive avatar. Acting as a compassionate third-party caretaker, the avatar leverages the psychological truth that humans naturally care better for others than for themselves—turning self-monitoring into an act of mutual responsibility.

The app guides non-medical crewmembers through daily wellness checks, features a smart One-Shot Consult to beat communication delays, and provides gentle, proactive notifications.

Why it matters: By humanizing health tracking through an approachable caretaker avatar, Spaceholder ensures early detection of physical and mental strain, reduces operational errors caused by burnout, and keeps crews resilient on deep-space journeys where medical help is far away.
details:
Spaceholder is an educational health self-monitoring and decision-support web app designed for astronauts on deep-space missions, such as a journey to Mars, where messages to Earth take up to 22 minutes one way.

Explore the Spaceholder Source Code & Live Demo:

Want to see how Spaceholder works under the hood? Check out our complete source code, project documentation, and simulated flight data in our GitHub repository:

https://github.com/eliasggs/2026-NASA-Space-Apps-Challenge

What does it do and how does it work?

Addressing NASA’s Distance from Earth and Isolation and Confinement hazards, Spaceholder replaces cold medical dashboards with a friendly caretaker avatar that guides astronauts through daily wellness routines:

  • Educational Daily Check-ins: Guides non-medical crewmembers through 6 key indicators (Heart Rate/HRV, Blood Pressure, Glucose, Temperature, Sleep, and Mood/PANAS), explaining why each metric shifts in microgravity and suggesting simple preventive actions (hydration, breathing, exercise, or rest).
  • Status Board & Interactive Body Map: Displays vital signs with NASA-sourced ranges, clickable body zones, and 7-day trend charts to catch subtle changes early.
  • Smart One-Shot Consult: Because every follow-up question from Earth costs up to 44 minutes in round-trip delay, the app asks key diagnostic questions upfront so one message carries complete medical context, while calculating Earth's reply window.
  • Guided Emergency Mode: Provides step-by-step emergency protocols with large buttons, a timer, and an action log.

What benefits does it have?

  • Overcomes Self-Neglect Bias: By using an empathetic third-party avatar, it leverages the psychological principle that people take better care of others than of themselves.
  • Empowers Non-Medical Crews: Translates space physiology into simple, actionable steps without needing a doctor on board.
  • Reduces Stress & Saves Time: Replaces alarming alerts with supportive guidance and compresses multi-turn medical consults into a single transmission.

What is the intended impact?

To detect physical fatigue, metabolic shifts, and emotional burnout early—preventing medical emergencies and operational errors during flight. This offline, delay-tolerant model can also support remote communities, maritime crews, and isolated areas on Earth without immediate hospital access.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.
  • Tools & Environment: Python, Pillow (asset processing), and Node.js.
  • Motion & Video: Adobe After Effects and Adobe Premiere Pro (avatar animations and pitch video).
  • AI: Gemini, motion16.com and Cloud services.
  • Web APIs & Deployment: MediaRecorder, getUserMedia, and GitHub Pages.
  • Simulated Flight Hardware Standards: Modeled after ISS CHeCS/HMS devices (Bio-Monitor/ECG Holter, i-STAT glucose analyzer, Actiwatch, clinical thermometers, and PANAS logs).

How is your project creative?

  1. Designing Around Delay: Makes the 22-minute communication delay the core design driver through the One-Shot Consult.
  2. Humanizing Telemetry: Uses a friendly caretaker avatar and gentle nudges to turn self-tracking into a supportive habit.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Crew Psychology: Isolation, disrupted circadian rhythms (16 sunrises/day), and the tendency to minimize personal symptoms.
  • Accessibility: High contrast, clear navigation, and status indicators that never rely on color alone.
  • Scientific Integrity: Grounded in verified NASA HRP and BHP sources, clearly separating spaceflight baselines from Earth ranges and functioning strictly as an educational prototype.
